teacher_issue: Which principle recognition is not full device analysis
scientific_teacher_note: Source B correctly identifies Bernoulli principle for the atomizer. However recognising a named principle is basic recall/understanding while official B44 requires Application-level analysis of real-world Bernoulli effects; do not automatically certify item for B44 exams.

teacher_issue: Text cites Figure6.10 without attached figure reference
scientific_teacher_note: Original printed NBF p101 Figure6.10 shows a simple atomizer and fast crossflow. Original GitHub Q2 has no referenceFigureId despite citing the figure. Source B is valid because fast air lowers local static pressure relative to the bottle, but verify the student-facing figure if used as a figure question.

teacher_issue: Droplet breakup versus pressure-driven suction
scientific_teacher_note: Source C is the best answer: nozzle/fast airflow helps break liquid into droplets. Distinguish the pressure difference that lifts liquid from fluid shear and breakup that form the spray; these are related but not identical Bernoulli mechanisms.

teacher_issue: Identify filter pump is a recognition question
scientific_teacher_note: NBF p101–102 discusses the water-jet filter pump. Source C is exactly the named device; nevertheless selecting a device name is recall, not independent Application-level analysis under B44. Retain in practice pending item-level certification.

teacher_issue: Side tube connection visually verified
scientific_teacher_note: The original printed NBF p101–102 text and Figure6.11 show the side tube connected to the vessel to evacuate. Original A matches; if using the figure in an exam, check that students can see labels clearly.

teacher_issue: Torricelli equation recognition versus solving problems
scientific_teacher_note: NBF p102 prints v=sqrt(2gh), so original C is right for ideal orifice efflux. The prepared key marks Knowledge; identifying a formula is not individually B40 Summative/Application, which requires applying the ideal energy model.

teacher_issue: Head is between surface and outlet
scientific_teacher_note: In the original printed Fig6.12 p102, h is the elevation difference between free surface and orifice, source C. Requires an open/atmospheric tank, sufficiently large reservoir, incompressible low-loss conditions and negligible free-surface speed for the simple formula.

teacher_issue: Negligible free-surface velocity
scientific_teacher_note: The textbook derives Torricelli by taking a large tank so v_surface≈0, source C. The top and outlet pressures are equal ambient pressure and losses neglected in the ideal model; real surface speed is not literally zero.

teacher_issue: Unit recall not Bernoulli summative Application
scientific_teacher_note: sqrt(gh) has SI dimensions m/s so source B is scientifically correct. But the teacher-prepared K tag and item task identify unit recall, not itself Application of Bernoulli for horizontal or vertical flow in official B40.

teacher_issue: Venturi meter usage versus analyzing mechanism
scientific_teacher_note: Original p103 defines a Venturi meter as a flow-speed/flow-rate device, so source C is correct. A purpose-only question may assess Understanding rather than B44 Application-level analysis; invite per-item cognitive review.

teacher_issue: Throat static-pressure decrease has ideal conditions
scientific_teacher_note: A narrow throat speeds an incompressible fluid under fixed discharge and lowers pressure in the steady inviscid horizontal same-streamline approximation, supporting source A. Real flow requires allowance for losses; original p103 diagram is idealized.

teacher_issue: Continuity equation rather than direct Bernoulli application
scientific_teacher_note: A1*v1=A2*v2 is correct for steady incompressible no-leak flow, source C. This is chiefly continuity outcome B36, not a direct B40 pressure-speed-height calculation or B44 device analysis; per-item SLO and cognition require teacher review.

teacher_issue: Figure6.13 piezometers not linked in GitHub record
scientific_teacher_note: Original printed NBF p103 Figure6.13 shows two columns of different height on wide/throat sections. These show static pressure head for the same liquid, source B. Q13 refers to the figure but GitHub has no referenceFigureId; verify visible correctly oriented student image before figure-based exam use.

teacher_issue: Correct pressure difference sign from Bernoulli
scientific_teacher_note: NBF p103 Eq6.25 supports P1−P2=(rho/2)*(v2²−v1²) for ideal horizontal flow. Source A has correct dimensions and sign; v2>v1 at throat gives P1>P2.

teacher_issue: Lift from integrated surface pressure distribution
scientific_teacher_note: The textbook p104–105 explains upward wing lift using pressure differences; source D is the best option. Real wing lift is a net aerodynamic force involving the full pressure/shear distribution and flow deflection, not solely a geometric path-length argument.

teacher_issue: Simplified Figure6.14 and no equal-transit-time rule
scientific_teacher_note: NBF printed p104 Fig6.14 labels faster flow/low pressure above the drawn aerofoil; source D matches that specific idealized figure. GitHub Q16 has no referenceFigureId despite asking about a diagram. Teach that equal transit times are NOT required for lift and do not generalize upper-side speed to every wing/flight condition.

teacher_issue: Magnus phenomenon identification is not full real-world analysis
scientific_teacher_note: NBF printed p105 shows spin-induced transverse force and flow asymmetry. Source C accurately identifies a moving spinning body, but identifying the condition is Understanding/recognition, not automatically B44 Application-level analysis of forces or trajectories.

teacher_issue: Spinning cricket ball example
scientific_teacher_note: Original p105 Magnus section discusses a spinning ball following a curved flight path, source B. Force direction depends on spin axis, velocity, surrounding air and flow; do not overclaim a universal bending direction from spin alone.

teacher_issue: Two-sheet activity is supportive Bernoulli effect
scientific_teacher_note: NBF p101 two-sheet activity depicts inward movement of sheets when blown between, source C; lower middle pressure than outside explains the net force. Standalone demonstration of Bernoulli effect is formative B39 context, not automatically individual summative B44 Application analysis.

teacher_issue: Printed Example6.4 correct but source item asks only its title/number
scientific_teacher_note: NBF printed p105 Example6.4 explicitly calculates pressure at a point 3m lower, with change of speed, giving 80.0 kPa. Source C matches the actual example number, but selecting the example label is Knowledge/lookup rather than B40 Application-level problem solving.
